faqs.question: Which sections does the page need, and in what order?
faqs.answer: Six blocks, in order: an opening line with her name, three to five captioned photos, four to six beats of your story, the question on a screen of its own, the yes and no buttons, and something behind the yes. That last one is the block people skip, and it is the one that stops the page feeling like a stunt.

faqs.question: Is a proposal page the same thing as a proposal website?
faqs.answer: In practice yes — both mean a one-page site built from a template and shared as a link. The word 'website' makes people think they need to build something from scratch, which is why ready-made templates exist.

faqs.question: Should I use the marriage proposal template if I am only asking her to be my girlfriend?
faqs.answer: Usually not. SubhSandesh's proposal template is titled 'Will You Marry Me?', so it overshoots a first ask. The 'I love you' page is the closer fit for this phrasing, and it is the platform's most-used page type at 1,138 pages, 24.9% of everything created platform-wide.

faqs.question: Does the no button really run away?
faqs.answer: On the proposal template the yes button grows each time the no is dodged. It is a joke, not a persuasion technique. Use it when you are already teasing each other and the answer is a formality, and turn it off when it is not.

faqs.question: What does she see in WhatsApp before she opens the link?
faqs.answer: A preview card with a title, a short description and a thumbnail image. That card is visible to anyone else in that chat, so keep the title neutral if the link might be seen over her shoulder or forwarded.

faqs.question: Can I stop other people from opening the page?
faqs.answer: Yes — set a password before you share it. 39.9% of SubhSandesh creators do this, measured platform-wide across all 16 page types (1,822 of 4,567 pages), which is roughly two in five.

faqs.question: How long does it take to make one?
faqs.answer: About forty-five minutes of real work if you have the photos ready. The median gap between first save and last edit on the platform is 6.4 hours, but that is sampled on the /love-gf template (n=1,138) and it measures elapsed time, not effort — most of it is people walking away and coming back.

faqs.question: Will it work on her phone?
faqs.answer: It opens in a mobile browser, so nothing needs installing. 48.9% of all page views on SubhSandesh happen on a phone (25,167 of 51,504 views, platform-wide), so the templates are built phone-first — but an old handset on patchy data will still struggle with five large photos.

faqs.question: Is there anything to add once she says yes?
faqs.answer: Something specific: a date, a time, a place, or a line you have not said out loud. A page that ends on confetti has nothing to say back to someone who just answered a question.

faqs.question: Is sending a link less meaningful than asking in person?
faqs.answer: If you are in the same room, yes — a link is a way of crossing a distance that is not there. A page earns its place when you are apart, or when you want her to have something she can reopen later.

faqs.question: What if she says no?
faqs.answer: Then the page should let her say it. Do not use the dodging no button if there is a real chance the answer is no; a button that will not accept her answer makes declining harder, not kinder, and she will remember that part.

faqs.question: Can I make one if I have never built a website?
faqs.answer: That is what the templates are for — you fill in text and photos and the page is generated for you. 92.7% of pages started on SubhSandesh are published and shared (4,234 of 4,567, platform-wide), which is a reasonable sign that people who start one finish it.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Will You Be My Girlfriend Proposal Page Online: What Goes On It

A "will you be my girlfriend" proposal page online is one web link you fill in and send: photos, a few lines, a question, a button. On SubhSandesh, 4,567 personalised pages have been created since 12 March 2026 across 16 page types, and 92.7% of every page started platform-wide gets published and shared (4,234 of 4,567) — the build is short enough that people actually finish it.

Another 39.9% of creators platform-wide lock the page with a password before they send it (1,822 of 4,567). This post covers the six blocks that go on the page, what the preview card looks like in her chat before she taps it, which of the two templates this exact phrasing really needs, and the cases where a page is the wrong way to ask.

## What is a "will you be my girlfriend" page, exactly?

It is a one-page website built from a template, personalised with your own photos and text, and handed over as a URL rather than an app or a file. She taps the link, the page opens in her phone browser, and she moves through it — scrolling, tapping, answering — instead of reading a paragraph in a chat bubble.

That difference in verb is the argument. A message is read; a page is opened.

Erika Pearson's 2007 study of [gift exchange in LiveJournal communities](https://firstmonday.org/ojs/index.php/fm/article/view/1835), published in *First Monday*, argued that digital gifts can work as a means of forming and maintaining social bonds and identity inside a virtual space, rather than as tokens shuttled between accounts. The page is the object; the chat is only the envelope.

## The six blocks that actually go on the page

Six, in the order the page is read: an opening line, three to five captioned photos, the story, the question on a screen of its own, the two buttons, and something behind the yes. Each block below gives what it is, what to put in it, how long it takes, and the mistake to avoid.

### 1. The opening line

The first thing she sees: one sentence, usually with her name in it. Put the shortest true thing you have — "Riya, I made you something" beats a paragraph.

Two minutes. The mistake is opening with the question itself; you have not earned it on screen one, and an answer that fast is a reflex, not a decision.

### 2. Three to five photos, one line each

Pictures of the two of you, each captioned with a single line of context. Three is enough and five is the ceiling before scrolling turns into work.

Ten to fifteen minutes, most of it spent choosing. The mistake is uploading twenty and captioning none: 48.9% of all page views platform-wide happen on a phone (25,167 of 51,504 views), and a phone shows one photo at a time.

### 3. The story, in order

Four to six beats — where you met, the thing she said that you still repeat, the day you noticed. This is what turns the page from a form into a made thing, and where most of your editing will go.

Twenty minutes. The mistake is writing a list of dates instead of a list of things that happened.

### 4. The question

One screen, one sentence, nothing else on it. "Will you be my girlfriend?" set on its own, with the photos and the story already behind it.

One minute to write, and the only block you should not be clever in. The mistake is burying the ask under a joke so that she has to guess whether you meant it.

### 5. The YES button, and the NO that dodges

The two buttons under the question. On SubhSandesh's proposal template the YES button grows every time the NO is dodged — use it only if you would both find it funny.

Thirty seconds. The mistake is taking the bit for persuasion: it is playful, not persuasive.

It is funny when the answer was always going to be yes and you already tease each other like this. It is obnoxious when she is genuinely undecided, because a button that will not let her say no is a page arguing with her. If you cannot tell which you are in, use two plain buttons.

### 6. What happens after she taps yes

The page should not stop at the tap. Put the next thing behind it — a date, a place, a time, a line you have not said out loud yet.

Five minutes. The mistake is ending on confetti: she just answered a question and the page has nothing to say back.

## What the link looks like in her chat before she taps it

Before any of the six blocks matter, she sees a preview card in the chat: a title, a short description, a thumbnail. That card decides whether the link is opened now or after dinner, and it is the only part of your page other people in that chat may also see.

Keep the title neutral if anyone might read over her shoulder. A 2025 paper in *Neophilology* on [the electronic greeting card as a polycode text](https://neophilology.elpub.ru/jour/article/view/531) analysed 159 cards — 110 collected from open-access sites and 49 sent in by respondents — and found the visual component consistently dominating the verbal one. She sees a picture and a name before she reads a word, so choose the thumbnail on purpose.

## /proposal or /love-gf: which template this phrasing actually wants

Usually /love-gf, not /proposal. "Will you be my girlfriend" is not a marriage proposal, and SubhSandesh's proposal template is literally titled "Will You Marry Me?" — a scrapbook of your story ending in that dodging YES button.

If you are already together and this is a milestone, or a re-ask, or you simply want the full scrapbook theatre, the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](/proposal) is the right build and the format carries it.

If you are asking someone who is not your partner yet, it overshoots badly. The ["I love you" page for a girlfriend or partner](/love-gf) is the honest recommendation: the same photo-and-line structure, a smaller frame, no marriage wording to explain away. It is also the most-used thing on the platform — 1,138 pages, 24.9% of everything created, and 16,362 views, 31.8% of all page views, both platform-wide figures.

And if you have not been on a date with her yet, neither one fits. The [date invitation page](/date-invitation) asks a smaller question, and a smaller question gets an easier yes.

| Template | Platform-wide rank by pages created | What the page asks | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| /love-gf | #1 — 1,138 pages, 24.9% of all pages | "I love you" | Someone who is not your partner yet |
| /apology-dashboard | #2 — 1,118 pages, 24.5% of all pages | "I'm sorry" | Asking again after the first attempt went badly |
| /proposal | Not in the published top five | "Will you marry me?" | Already a couple, or you want the scrapbook and the YES-button bit |
| /date-invitation | Not in the published top five | "Come out with me" | You have not had a first date yet |

Two rows carry a page count and two do not: SubhSandesh publishes its top five page types, and neither /proposal nor /date-invitation is in it.

## Who can see the page once you have sent it

Anyone who has the link. A shared page is a URL, and a URL travels. 39.9% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing it (1,822 of 4,567) — two in five, measured platform-wide across all 16 page types, because there is no proposal-specific breakdown to quote and inventing one would be worse than admitting that.

Set a password if the link could be forwarded, screenshotted into a group chat, or opened on a shared laptop. The answer is hers to give privately; a page anyone with the link can read turns it into a small public event.

## When a page is the wrong way to ask

Four cases, and the first is the common one: you are in the same room. A link crosses a distance, and there is no distance here — the page becomes a stunt, and she will notice you picked the harder-to-ignore format over simply saying it.

Three more cases where this loses. She has already told you she is not interested, and a page does not reopen that: it only makes declining more awkward, and the dodging-NO bit turns actively unkind.

Her phone is old or her data is patchy, and five photos will stall on the way in. Or she is simply not someone who enjoys being surprised on the internet — some people find a personalised page delightful and some find it exposing, and you already know which one she is.

A 2026 meta-analysis in *BMC Psychology* of [behavioural antecedents of virtual gifting](https://bmcpsychology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40359-026-04813-x), synthesising studies published between 2015 and 2025, reported that gifting was positively associated with engagement, social acceptance and perceived value, and negatively associated with passing time. Gifts land with people who are already leaning in, not with people idly scrolling. A proposal page is the same bet.

## How long the build actually takes

Set aside about forty-five minutes of real work: choosing photos, writing six to eight lines, setting a password, opening the finished link on your own phone to check it. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.4 hours — but that number is sampled on /love-gf (n=1,138), not on proposal pages, and it measures elapsed time rather than effort. People start, walk away, come back and fix one line.

Coming back is the point. Klug and Qiu's 2021 paper in *AoIR Selected Papers of Internet Research* on [motivations for virtual gift-giving in Douyin live streams](https://spir.aoir.org/ojs/index.php/spir/article/view/12194), built on twelve semi-structured interviews, found senders used virtual gifts mainly as a social means of appreciation and expected nothing in return — yet they noticed and valued the small gesture that came back. Whatever she taps, answer her on the page.

## Sources

- Pearson, ["Digital gifts: gift exchange in Livejournal communities"](https://firstmonday.org/ojs/index.php/fm/article/view/1835), *First Monday* 12(5), 7 May 2007
- Savelyeva, ["The electronic greeting card as a polycode text"](https://neophilology.elpub.ru/jour/article/view/531), *Neophilology* 11(3), 16 October 2025
- ["Virtual gifting as affective monetization"](https://bmcpsychology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40359-026-04813-x), *BMC Psychology*, 3 June 2026
- Klug and Qiu, ["Virtual gift-giving in Douyin live streams"](https://spir.aoir.org/ojs/index.php/spir/article/view/12194), *AoIR Selected Papers of Internet Research*, 15 September 2021

SubhSandesh figures are first-party, measured 2026-09-17, platform-wide across all 16 page types except the 6.4-hour edit gap, which is sampled on /love-gf.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific first-party data exists. A read-only probe of the `proposalpages` collection was refused by this machine's production-read policy in wave 1 and again in this wave, so every SubhSandesh figure in the body is labelled in prose as either platform-wide across all 16 page types or sampled on /love-gf (n=1,138). No number anywhere in this post is attributed to proposal pages.

The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty, so this post states and implies no price, no free tier and no paid tier. The words free, cost, price, paid, tier and ₹ do not appear in the body at all. This is a deliberate omission on a keyword where at least one measured incumbent (pixeryhub.com) leads its titles with 'Free', per content/keywords/2026-09-16-propose-100/competitor-map.md; whether the other nine results do the same was not verifiable, and the earlier claim that the entire SERP leads with price has been removed for that reason. It remains the one thing a reader may want that this post does not answer. Closes when facts.md carries a pricing block.

Phase 1 was inherited, not freshly measured. WebSearch is exhausted for this session (200/200), so the competitor table in the research brief is transcribed from content/keywords/2026-09-16-propose-100/serps.md, measured 2026-09-16 and India-served. No competitor page was fetched or read in full for this post, and no position is described as current.

Full text was not read for any of the four sources. All four claims come from the abstract or the article landing page: firstmonday.org and spir.aoir.org HTML/PDF galleys returned empty bodies, bmcpsychology.biomedcentral.com returns a JavaScript challenge (abstract read via the Europe PMC REST API instead), and the Neophilology full text is a Russian-language PDF (abstract read in Russian on the publisher page and in English via Crossref).

The single best subject-fit source available — Petrelli & Whittaker, 'Family memories in the home: contrasting physical and digital mementos' — sits on the wave-1 banned URL list (shura.shu.ac.uk/2907) and was dropped for that reason, not on quality. mdpi.com and journals.sagepub.com both held usable papers but were already at 2 posts in this batch with siblings writing concurrently, so they were dropped rather than risk pushing a domain past the 3-post cap.

failed.why: STRUCTURAL — two rules inside references/page-structure.md collide. Block 7 mandates "a sources list with links and publication dates, as a final H2"; the Heading rules require "every H2 section must be answerable on its own in 2-3 sentences". A bibliography is a reference list, not a question, so the mandated '## Sources' H2 cannot satisfy the heading rule, and the heading rule cannot be satisfied without deleting a mandated block. Every other H2 was re-checked in this fix pass and now opens with a self-contained 2-3 sentence answer; three did not before it — 'The six blocks that actually go on the page' opened on meta-text about the block format, '/proposal or /love-gf' opened on the throat-clear 'Here is the uncomfortable part', and 'When a page is the wrong way to ask' opened on a single case rather than the count — and all three were rewritten to answer first. Closes only when page-structure.md exempts Block 7 from the heading rule or moves the sources list below H2 level; that is a reference-file change, not an article change.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page in the 2026-09-16 measurement of this SERP that describes the artefact from the recipient's side — the chat preview card, the first screen, the after-yes screen, who else can open the URL — and the only one that tells the reader this phrasing probably wants the 'I love you' page rather than a marry-me scrapbook. That second claim is an inference from what the ten measured results sell, not from reading them: no competitor page was fetched, so nothing here asserts what any incumbent currently says or what year sits in their titles. The 39.9% password-protection and 92.7% publish-and-share rates are unavailable to any competitor, and naming the dodging-NO button as a joke that turns unkind is the kind of tradeoff answer engines favour. Against that: the 2026-09-16 run judged 8 of 10 results weak, and the ones that hold the top slots are small product pages serving transactional intent, while this is an article rather than a builder — a searcher who wants a link generator will bounce, and that is the likeliest outcome. The post also answers nothing about what the product costs, because the facts.md pricing block is empty; the competitor map records pixeryhub.com leading its titles with 'Free', and whether the other nine do the same was not verifiable. 46 articles in this exact territory already live on this domain, and that same run found subhsandesh.in nowhere in the top 20 of any of the 11 SERPs, so this post competes with its own corpus for internal relevance with no evidence the corpus ranks at all. Ranking takes months and depends on authority and links, and none of that is predicted here. On the measured evidence this post does not beat the top five: those five serve a transactional intent with a product, and this is prose.
